precepts.text: Israel and Judah were oppressed together, and all that took them captive held them fast and refused to let them go.
precepts.point: He executes judgment for the oppressed, gives food to the hungry, and looses the prisoners. We are the prisoners, prisoners of hope bound here in Babylon. If you do not think we are prisoners and want to go back to Africa or to the homeland, which is Jerusalem in northeast Africa, go find a boat or a plane ticket and try to produce a passport; that passport is your permission slip. Just because you do not have chains on your neck, do not be fooled that we are not bound here.

note.label: Psalm 146: The Most High Looses the Prisoners

precepts.why:
“The Lord looseth the prisoners”. We are the prisoners, prisoners of hope bound here in Babylon. “The children of Israel and the children of Judah were oppressed together: and all that took them captives held them fast; they refused to let them go.”

If you do not think we are prisoners and want to go back to Africa or to the homeland, which is Jerusalem in northeast Africa, go find a boat or a plane ticket and try to produce a passport; that passport is your permission slip. Just because you do not have chains on your neck, do not be fooled that we are not bound here. They hold us fast and refuse to let us go.

precepts.text: The Most High raised up Pharaoh to show His power and declare His name throughout all the earth; the oppressor has that same mindset, that he will not let us go, because he likes us weak and our people destroyed so he remains on top.

note.label: Psalm 146: The Most High Looses the Prisoners

precepts.why: “For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.” The Most High raised up Pharaoh to show his power and declare his name throughout all the earth. The oppressor today has that same mindset, that he will not let us go, because he likes us weak and our people destroyed so he remains on top. And the Most High executeth judgment for the oppressed and looseth the prisoners.

We are still found in their hand, prisoners bound here in Babylon, and the one who executeth judgment for the oppressed is the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 146: The Most High Looses the Prisoners

precepts.why: “He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.” We are the saints, the Israelites. The ones who led us into captivity shall go into captivity; that is the judgment for the oppressed, and the Most High loosing the prisoners. Until then, here is our patience and our faith.

The Old Testament goes into Joseph and how he's imprisoned in Egypt; so Psalms 146. “Which executeth judgment for the oppressed: which giveth food to the hungry. The Lord looseth the prisoners:” Which executeth judgment for the oppressed: that's not everybody on the planet. So all this goes into gospel.

Start at verse 5: “Happy is he that hath the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in the Lord his God: Which made heaven, and earth, the sea, and all that therein is: which keepeth truth for ever:” So remember, this is talking about the people of Jacob, because it says he's the God of Jacob. Which executeth judgment for the oppressed, letting you know that Jacob's children would be oppressed. Which giveth food to the hungry: Jacob's children would need food, physical and spiritual. The Lord looseth the prisoners: Jacob's children would be prisoners.
